about: Signal sources as DATA: how an item maps to fields, which items are kept (filters) and which signals of need add to a score. Every number and word is a knob of the row; a person's own rows replace these through `source_row`. A source with a `request` reads one public address; candidates behind a login arrive as `items` from the person's connection tool, and no row holds a credential. `group` gathers rows a workflow reads together (`launches`: where new products launch; `vendors`: vendors compared on proof they publish); a new launch source or a new proof measure is a new row, never code.

records.label: Companies whose job post has stayed open
records.meaning: A role that has stayed open for weeks at a small company shows a problem it has not solved inside, and budget set aside for it. The post's own list of day-to-day duties says what is broken.

signals.says: The post has been open for 30 days or more.
The post has been open for 21 days or more.

records.label: Local businesses in a place, scored by what their reviews say
records.meaning: A business whose customers keep naming one delay, or whose reviews suddenly pick up, has told you what it needs. Candidates for a place come from the person's map data connection as `items`.

signals.says: Reviews mention slow quotes.
A large share of the reviews are from the last 90 days.
At least 5 reviews came in during the last 90 days.

records.label: Show HN posts launched in the last day
records.meaning: A Show HN post is a maker launching to builders; points and comments in its first hours show whether it lands. Read from the public Hacker News search address, no account needed.

signals.says: It launched less than an hour ago: the window to out-launch it is widest now.
It launched within the last six hours.
It already has at least 20 points: people are paying attention to it.
At least 10 people commented on it.

records.label: Products launched on Product Hunt in the last day
records.meaning: A Product Hunt launch day is a public race for upvotes; the first hours decide its rank. Its API needs the person's own token, so the launches arrive as `items` from the person's Product Hunt connection.

signals.says: It launched less than an hour ago: the window to out-launch it is widest now.
It launched within the last six hours.
It already has at least 100 upvotes: people are paying attention to it.
At least 20 people commented on it.

records.label: Y Combinator company launches in the last day
records.meaning: A YC launch post is a funded company announcing a product to an audience of buyers and investors. The list arrives as `items` from the person's own reader of the launches page.

signals.says: It launched less than an hour ago: the window to out-launch it is widest now.
It launched within the last six hours.
It already has at least 50 votes: people are paying attention to it.

records.label: Launch posts on X in the last day
records.meaning: A founder's launch post on X spreads by reposts in its first hours. X needs the person's own account, so posts that announce a launch arrive as `items` from the person's X connection (for example a search for 'launching today').

signals.says: It launched less than an hour ago: the window to out-launch it is widest now.
It launched within the last six hours.
It already has at least 200 likes: people are paying attention to it.
At least 30 people commented on it.
At least 50 people reposted it.

records.label: Public repositories created in the last day that are drawing stars
records.meaning: An open-source launch shows in a new repository's stars in its first hours. Read from GitHub's public search address; {since} is the date to search from, such as 2026-11-01.

signals.says: It launched less than an hour ago: the window to out-launch it is widest now.
It launched within the last six hours.
It already has at least 50 stars: people are paying attention to it.

records.label: Vendors in a category, scored only on proof they publish
records.meaning: A 'best X for Y' comparison earns citations when every score can be checked. Each metric is a number someone can verify at a public address (a status page, a review site, a published price, a named customer story); price_published is 1 when the price is on the vendor's own site and 0 when it is not; a metric with no proof address is sent as null, so it refuses the filters or stays quiet and never counts as zero. A sponsored vendor is scored by the same row as everyone else: sponsorship is a label on the page, never a field here. Vendors arrive as `items`, gathered by the comparison workflow; every threshold is the person's to change for their category.

signals.says: At least 5 customers are named in public case studies.
At least 100 public reviews on an independent review site.
Rated 4.5 or more out of 5 on that review site.
Its public status page shows 99.9% uptime or more over the last 90 days.
Its price is published on its own site, no sales call needed.
It publishes at least one independent security attestation (such as a SOC 2 report or an ISO 27001 certificate).
It shipped a public release in the last 30 days.
